resources.string: Connect this phone directly to your bottle over Bluetooth. Sip records stay on the phone and are written to Health Connect—no Home Assistant or Hidrate cloud account is required.
Filled by scanning; not used as identity

Select the bottle, then start this 90-second test. Leave it still for 20 seconds, take a sip and immediately tap “Mark sip”, then wait 20 seconds, move it without drinking and tap “Mark movement”. Keep the official Hidrate app closed.
Scan for your bottle, confirm its capacity, then start live sync.
No bottle was found. Wake it by moving it, make sure the official app is closed, and try again. You can also enter its Bluetooth address manually.

HidrateSpark Health Sync requests write-only access to hydration and Nearby Devices access for your bottle. It stores sip time and volume locally, writes those records to Health Connect, and does not read other health data. It has no Internet permission, analytics, advertising, cloud service, or Home Assistant dependency.
